title: Disable fabricated PG-2 sample attestation
summary: Remove the debug PG-2 auto-attestation generator and make its legacy harness fail closed before launching or writing evidence.
reason: Remediate P1 AUDIT-FIND-W09-008. The automation authored exact media-validation claims from caller paths and fixed narrative instead of current backend/filesystem provenance.
behavior_before: Debug automation accepted arbitrary source/output paths and decision text, hard-coded successful media checks and exact route/publish/ActiveJobs claims, then appended a sample_validation_record.v1 without proving those facts.
behavior_after: The Tauri debug shell supports only the PG-2 WebView launch automation; it has no sample-validation request generator. The obsolete append harness always returns a nonzero actionable error before launching Tauri/backend/pipeline or writing a record, and directs operators to backend preview plus the operator-controlled WebView append flow.
tests_added: A static Rust test forbids the removed automation mode, request generator, append route, exact-path proof, and hard-coded successful FFmpeg check.
A subprocess test passes nonexistent media paths and Decision=accepted, requires a nonzero refusal, and proves no sample-validation log is created.
The Tauri scaffold now requires the legacy harness to advertise the disabled flow and forbids fabricated proof fields or append/launch routes.

rollback_plan: Revert the debug automation removal, fail-closed wrapper, operator guide, tests, generated summaries/maps, and packet together. Do not restore the former hard-coded attestation generator without a backend-authored run-bound evidence projection and its required validation.
notes: This is a refusal-only safety remediation: it removes an invalid evidence producer and does not add a new acceptance path. No source/output media is read or mutated; no pipeline, backend, append, publish, or cleanup command runs. Representative real-media validation is therefore not required for this batch. Future restoration of automation is a separate high-risk task requiring backend evidence binding and representative source/output hash/playback validation.
